briefings.title: A new era of discovery: AI and the frontiers of science with Demis Hassabis
briefings.tldr: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis predicts that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) will arrive between 2029 and 2031, ushering in a transformative "singularity" era marked by self-improving code, agentic systems, and a massive 100x acceleration of scientific and medical discovery.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis predicts that Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) will arrive between 2029 and 2031, ushering in a transformative "singularity" era marked by self-improving code, agentic systems, and a massive 100x acceleration of scientific and medical discovery.

---

## The Path and Timeline to AGI
* **AGI Arrival Horizon:** Hassabis projects AGI will be realized around 2030 (specifically within the 2029–2031 window). 
* **The "Einstein Test" for AGI:** While current models show "jagged intelligence," true AGI will require a leap of conceptual insight.
  * *The Benchmark:* Hassabis defines this as giving a model a knowledge cutoff of 1901 and evaluating whether it can independently formulate the conceptual leaps Albert Einstein did in 1905, such as special relativity.
* **Feeling the Shift:** Hassabis notes the approach of AGI is already palpable. He cites "vibe coding" game prototypes in his spare time in just 1–2 hours—tasks that previously required up to six months of manual engineering.
* **The Singularity:** Hassabis describes this impending era as the most transformative invention in human history, making long-term predictions beyond its arrival point nearly impossible.

## Google's Edge in the "Ferocious" AI Race
* **The Full-Stack Advantage:** Hassabis asserts Google is the only organization in the world operating a complete feedback loop across the entire AI pipeline:
  * Proprietary custom chips (TPUs) and specialized data centers.
  * Scaled cloud infrastructure.
  * A world-class frontier research bench (Google DeepMind).
  * Direct distribution channels reaching billions of consumers.
* **Rapid Scale and Adoption:** Google's streamlined, "agent-first" tech stack has allowed it to deploy powerful, efficient models directly to massive user bases.
  * *Milestones:* The Gemini App now boasts 900 million monthly active users, alongside massive deployments of AI Overviews in Search.
* **A Broad Research Bench:** Hassabis points to Google's diverse research capabilities—developing media generation models like Omni and highly efficient, performant models like Gemini 1.5 Flash and Pro—as its ultimate competitive edge.

## Societal Impact, "100x" Acceleration, and the Industry Backlash
* **The 100x Industrial Revolution:** Hassabis estimates AI's impact will be 10 times greater than the Industrial Revolution and occur 10 times faster (occurring over a decade rather than a century). 
* **Democratization of Opportunity:** AI tools lower the barrier to creation, allowing a single motivated individual or a 1-to-2-person startup to build what once required a team of 50 specialized software engineers.
* **Addressing Public Backlash:** Hassabis believes the AI industry must combat growing public anxiety and "tech backlash" by prioritizing and demonstrating unequivocal, concrete societal benefits. 
  * *Key Areas:* The main counterweight to public skepticism is applying AI to hard science challenges, such as drug discovery, climate mitigation, materials science, and clean energy.
* **A Cautious Optimist Philosophy:** Rejecting extreme positions of both "doomers" and pure "accelerationists," Hassabis argues for taking a measured approach to AGI. He emphasizes that society must give itself the time to implement safety, security, and robust guardrails over the next few years.

## AI for Science: From AlphaFold to World Models
* **The AlphaFold Paradigm Shift:** Hassabis recounts a pivotal decision filmed for the documentary *The Thinking Game*. Instead of setting up a standard web portal where scientists submitted individual genetic sequences for protein-folding predictions, DeepMind chose to run every known protein in existence (over 200 million) and release the entire database for free to the global scientific community.
* **Simulations and "Genie":** Simulations are critical for both teaching AI systems and generating safe training data.
  * *Real-World Testing:* Google is utilizing "Genie"—an interactive 3D world model—to safely simulate extreme, "one-in-a-billion" edge cases for Waymo autonomous vehicles (e.g., simulating forest fires or wild animals on the road).
  * *Complex Systems:* DeepMind's weather forecasting models can predict extreme events, like Hurricane Beryl, much faster and more accurately than traditional fluid dynamics equations.
* **The Next Technical Step-Changes:** Leading labs are heavily investing in several critical evolutionary steps for models:
  * *Self-Improvement:* Developing coding and mathematics agents where outputs are easily verifiable, creating a self-reinforcing flywheel.
  * *Continuous Learning:* Moving past static post-training cutoffs so models can adapt and learn dynamically after release.
  * *Consistency:* Eliminating "jagged" performance profiles so models do not fail on simple, out-of-distribution variations of tasks they otherwise excel at.

## Builder Advice: Direction over Velocity
* **The Warning on Freneticism:** While praising the unparalleled builder energy of Silicon Valley, Hassabis cautions that extreme "freneticism" can inhibit deep, long-term scientific thinking.
* **The Velocity Vector:** Hassabis warns developers and founders against favoring speed over direction.
  * *Reflective Thinking:* For deep-tech breakthroughs that take years to yield results, ensuring the correct strategic direction is far more critical than raw speed.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "When we look back at this time, I think we will realize we were standing in the foothills of the singularity." — Sir Demis Hassabis

> "If you want to try and quantify it, it’s going to be 10 times the impact of the Industrial Revolution, maybe 10 times faster... So you can think of it as 100x the Industrial Revolution, and that might be an underestimate." — Sir Demis Hassabis

> "Making sure you have the direction right is often more important than just the speed... If you’re running 100 miles an hour in the wrong direction, that’s actually worse than standing still and taking a moment to think about getting the direction right." — Sir Demis Hassabis

briefings.title: Andrej Karpathy Joins Anthropic | SpaceX Files S1: How Does it Trade | Cerebras Smashes Day 1
briefings.tldr: As elite AI firms like Anthropic and OpenAI command staggering private valuations and push compute grants directly to startups, legacy SaaS companies face a structural squeeze, compounded by a looming public and political backlash over AI-driven white-collar layoffs.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
As elite AI firms like Anthropic and OpenAI command staggering private valuations and push compute grants directly to startups, legacy SaaS companies face a structural squeeze, compounded by a looming public and political backlash over AI-driven white-collar layoffs.

---

## The AI Giants: Valuation Wars and Token Ecosystems

*   **Anthropic’s $900 Billion Valuation Leap:** Anthropic is in talks to raise $30 billion at a $900 billion valuation (up from $380 billion in February), backed by investors like Green Oaks, Sequoia, Alimter, and Dragoneer. 
    *   **Low-Risk Trade:** Investors view this as a highly secure "post-IPO" trade because the business model is entirely derisked from existential and IPO failure; the only remaining variable is valuation risk.
    *   **Dario Amodei vs. Sam Altman:** Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, favors clean, low-drama, straight-cash transactions completed in days. In contrast, OpenAI's Sam Altman pushes complex financial engineering (e.g., mixing upfront cash, contingent venture debt, and SoftBank loans) to maximize valuations.
*   **The Reality of Enterprise Token Spend:** Salesforce spent $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year, primarily for engineering and code generation. 
    *   **Cost Per Head:** This translates to roughly $15,000 to $20,000 per year per developer—representing only 4% of an engineer's fully burdened $500,000 salary.
    *   **The TAM Conundrum:** For OpenAI and Anthropic to hit their projected $1 trillion token revenue targets, they must capture 20% of global corporate R&D/engineering payrolls. If enterprises do not replace or supplement a fifth of their engineering salary budgets with tokens, current foundation model valuations will face severe corrections.
*   **OpenAI’s Y Combinator Offensive:** OpenAI is offering $2 million in tokens to every startup in the current Y Combinator batch in exchange for equity.
    *   **Valuation Inflation:** This massive capital injection is expected to drive up seed round valuations (potentially anchoring them at $60 million to $100 million post-demo day) and dramatically shrink the ownership share available to traditional early-stage VCs.
    *   **Capacity Signal:** This move suggests OpenAI currently holds surplus compute capacity, whereas Anthropic remains heavily capacity-constrained.

---

## Public SaaS Bifurcation: Winners vs. "Terminal" Legacy Players

*   **The Rebound of Software Giants:** Top-tier SaaS companies are demonstrating strong acceleration, proving that a broader software creation boom is underway.
    *   **Data Dog:** Reported its first $1 billion revenue quarter (growing 32% year-over-year) and crossed $4 billion in ARR.
    *   **Figma:** Accelerated for its second consecutive quarter, reaching a two-year high Net Dollar Retention (NDR) of 139%. 
    *   **Figma's Missed Pipeline:** Despite its strong quarter, Figma missed a massive $500 million opportunity by failing to natively build a design-to-production pipeline (leaving space for startups like Replit and Lovable).
*   **The Terminal Decline of Wix and Squarespace:** Wix has plummeted 45% since its recent stock buyback, dropping to a $2.2 billion market cap and trading at roughly 1x revenue. 
    *   **The Double-Squeeze:** Legacy website builders are being decimated by "vibe coding" tools on the low end (allowing non-technical users to generate sites via prompts) and Shopify on the high end, which has successfully captured the merchant and e-commerce markets.
*   **The Futility of Defensive Stock Buybacks:** Heavy criticism was aimed at companies like Wix and Salesforce for executing massive stock buybacks to appease activist investors. Preserving cash balance sheets is deemed far more valuable for strategic AI acquisitions in a fast-evolving tech environment.

---

## Compute Starvation and the Infrastructure Supercycle

*   **Hardware and Optical Connects on Fire:** While traditional legacy software faces downward valuation pressure, the physical hardware sector—semiconductors, optical connections, and power infrastructure (e.g., SanDisk, Marvell, Micron, Broadcom, Cisco)—is experiencing a historic boom.
*   **Nebius and the Capex Bottleneck:** Nebius is accelerating at 684% growth due to acute compute starvation. 
    *   **Bureaucratic Salvation:** The slow permitting and construction of modern data centers may protect the industry from overcapacity. If data center rollouts are delayed while corporate token spend remains stable, compute will remain scarce, keeping margins high for providers like Nebius and CoreWeave.
*   **The VC Capex Trap:** Building competitive infrastructure startups now requires $500 million to $1 billion in upfront capex. Consequently, seed-stage investors are increasingly avoiding early-stage infrastructure deals due to the extreme capital intensity required to survive.

---

## The $1.75 Trillion SpaceX IPO

*   **The S1 Financial Lag:** SpaceX has targeted June 12th for a historic IPO, aiming for a $1.75 trillion valuation and a $75 billion raise, with 30% of the float allocated to retail investors.
    *   **Outdated Financials:** The initial S1 prospectus will only reflect December financials ($15B–$18B revenue, 20%–30% growth for Starlink/SpaceX standalone). It will fail to reflect major 2024 events, including the consolidation of X.AI, the Cursor acquisition, and the Anthropic deal.
*   **Speculative "Casino" Pricing:** Retail enthusiasm and Robinhood-style "meme" trading could decouple the stock from traditional discounted cash flow (DCF) metrics. The panel predicts the valuation could quickly spike to $3 trillion or $5 trillion based purely on retail demand before experiencing a sharp correction.

---

## The Looming Political and Social Backlash Against Tech

*   **Euphemistic Layoffs and "Political Morons":** Tech leaders are implementing aggressive workforce reductions (Meta laying off 8,000; Cisco cutting 4,000; Intuit shedding 1,600) while publicly attributing these cuts to AI efficiencies. 
    *   **Standard Chartered:** The bank’s CEO notoriously framed eliminating 7,800 jobs not as losses, but as "job reductions in favor of the machines."
*   **The PR Failure of AI Founders:** Unlike previous tech waves (like Meta/Facebook pretending to "bring the world together"), AI founders have spent three years hyping AGI's ability to destroy jobs and humanity, leading to immediate public hostility and events like Eric Schmidt being booed at a college graduation.
*   **The "Social Charter" Mandate:** To avoid punitive wealth taxes and severe political backlashes, major tech companies may soon face a "social obligation" to artificially reinflate their headcounts and employ thousands of workers, even if AI agents can technically perform those roles.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Once you lose that veneer, you are going to be valued for the rest of your life on some variety of revenue growth and cash flow... It’s almost impossible to ever get back to 50 times ARR again."  
> — **Rory**

> "We have people who are brilliant scientists who politically are utter morons. And the people who are utter morons at AI but brilliant at politics are going to have us for lunch. That’s the movie of the next three years."  
> — **Rory**

> "At least when Meta was busy destroying the world, they were smart enough to pretend it was all about bringing friends together and not destroying democracy. We will regret that lack of transparency."  
> — **Rory**

> "Politics when you've been laid off by email at 4:00 AM because the CEO of your company has decided he'd prefer to buy $100 million of machines than $100 million of people... that politics becomes very different."  
> — **Jason Lemkin**

briefings.title: Beyond the keynote with Sundar Pichai
briefings.tldr: At Google I/O 2026, Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the industry's shift toward agentic workflows and the critical need for cost-efficient "workhorse" models like Gemini 3.5 Flash.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
At Google I/O 2026, Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted the industry's shift toward agentic workflows and the critical need for cost-efficient "workhorse" models like Gemini 3.5 Flash. He emphasized that managing the rapid evolution of AI requires balancing open-source collaboration with responsible safety protocols while navigating systemic global compute bottlenecks.

---

## The Rise of AI Agents and User Trust
* **Agentic Workflows:** Developer-led workflows have evolved from basic code auto-completion to full agent orchestration. 
    * During the event, Google demonstrated this capability in "Anti-Gravity" for building an operating system, proving that agents can handle highly complex, multi-step environments.
* **The Shared Trust Journey:** Building trust in AI agents mirrors the societal adoption of email spam filters or self-driving cars like Waymo.
    * **Deliberate Integration:** To ensure safety, Google is slowly integrating its powerful Gemini Spark engine with first-party services (Gmail, Calendar) before exposing full browser use, computer use, and third-party integrations via the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
* **Automation vs. Delight:** AI agents will increasingly handle tedious administrative "chores" (such as renewing a DMV license). This shift is intended to free up human users to focus on aspects of the internet that offer genuine exploration, joy, and direct connection with creators.

## Cybersecurity and Model Deployment Paradigms
* **CodeMender Launch:** Google introduced CodeMender, an internal tool now being deployed externally that continuously monitors for vulnerabilities, generates patches, tests them, and deploys updates 24/7 in real time.
* **Strategic Acquisitions:** Google's integration of its Wiz acquisition provides state-of-the-art, real-time vulnerability monitoring to reinforce cloud infrastructure security.
* **Responsible Disclosure:** Addressing frontier cyber-capable models (such as Anthropic's Mitheos and OpenAI's GPT-5.5 Cyber), Pichai advocated for a measured deployment strategy.
    * Google favors established security practices, such as its "Project Zero" framework, which gives vendors a 90-day window to patch vulnerabilities before public disclosure.
    * **The Threshold for Release:** Deployment decisions should be made on a model-by-model basis. A 1% to 2% improvement over the state-of-the-art warrants standard release, whereas 20% "generational jumps" require deep coordination with government and industry safety bodies.

## Open Source Viability and Global Competition
* **The Gemma Ecosystem:** Google remains committed to open source with its release of Gemma 4, but Pichai noted that the immense Capex and R&D costs required to build frontier models necessitate a balanced approach between open and closed architectures.
* **The Rise of Chinese Open Source:** Regarding highly efficient Chinese models like DeepSeek, Pichai argued that enterprise clients select models based on reliability, predictability, and safety rather than geographic origin.
    * He emphasized that rather than fearing foreign open-source tech, the United States must focus on maintaining its own lead at the technological frontier.
* **Dynamic Software Architecture:** Because AI technology is evolving rapidly, enterprises must design their technical stacks to be modular, allowing them to dynamically swap underlying models as the ecosystem shifts.

## The Economics of AI: Workhorse Models and Compute Bottlenecks
* **Gemini 3.5 Flash:** Designed specifically to curb ballooning enterprise AI budgets, the Flash class of models acts as a cost-efficient "workhorse."
    * **High-Speed Efficiency:** Flash is optimized for high-frequency agentic loops, with demos showing it running at speeds of up to 800 tokens per second.
* **The Compute Deficit:** Google operates in a state of constant compute deficit, where demand heavily outstrips capacity. This scarcity forces continuous trade-offs between scaling massive, capability-maximizing "Ultra" models and serving efficient "Flash" models to billions of users.
* **Multilayered Bottlenecks:** Pichai noted that solving one bottleneck simply exposes another. Google is actively managing parallel constraints across physical data center permitting, local power grid access, rising memory/component costs, and specialized silicon manufacturing.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "I do expect agents to be a core part of how we work... [but] it'll allow humans to use the internet in ways that give them joy and purpose and not always be forced to deal with 'I have to fill these 18 form fields to renew a DMV license.'" 
> — Sundar Pichai

> "The more AI becomes advanced, the more it's a societal conversation versus a single company conversation."
> — Sundar Pichai

> "If you think something is a bottleneck and you solve it, something else becomes the bottleneck... there are systemic bottlenecks across all layers of the stack now."
> — Sundar Pichai

briefings.title: Building the quantum-AI future with Hartmut Neven and James Manyika

people.name: James Manyika
people.role: SVP of Research, Technology, and Society, Google

briefings.tldr: Google’s Quantum AI division is rapidly accelerating its timeline toward commercial viability, demonstrating breakthroughs in below-threshold error correction and quantum machine learning that lower the hardware threshold for practical applications and mandate a transition to post-quantum encryption by 2029.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Google’s Quantum AI division is rapidly accelerating its timeline toward commercial viability, demonstrating breakthroughs in below-threshold error correction and quantum machine learning that lower the hardware threshold for practical applications and mandate a transition to post-quantum encryption by 2029.

## The Foundations and Hardware of Google Quantum AI
* **Superposition as a Superpower:** Quantum computing derives its processing capabilities from superposition—the ability of a quantum system to exist in multiple configurations simultaneously.
    * **The Willow Chip:** Google's 105-qubit Willow chip can process $2^{105}$ configurations in a single clock cycle, completing calculations in minutes that would take a classical supercomputer 10 septillion years.
* **Superconducting Architecture:** Google builds macroscopic qubits using loops of superconducting wire (Josephson circuits). This allows quantum phenomena to be engineered at a macroscopic scale rather than attempting to manipulate individual microscopic atoms.
    * **Ultra-Cold Engineering:** To eliminate thermal noise, Google's quantum chips are cooled to **10 millikelvin** (one-hundredth of a degree above absolute zero), making the environment colder than deep space.
* **Exploration of Alternative Pathways:** While Google's primary path utilizes superconducting qubits, the company has established a new laboratory in Boulder, Colorado, to pursue a **neutral atom approach**. This parallel track may offer distinct advantages in quantum-enhanced sensing.

## Key Milestones and Algorithmic Breakthroughs
* **The Error Correction Hurdle:** Keeping fragile superposition states alive (coherence time) is the key challenge of quantum hardware. Google has extended coherence times from 20 microseconds to over 250 microseconds.
    * **Below-Threshold Breakthrough:** In 2024, the Willow chip demonstrated a twofold reduction in errors when physical qubits were scaled up to form a logical qubit. This "below-threshold" milestone proved that physical scaling successfully suppresses errors.
* **Accelerating the Commercial Roadmap:** Algorithmic advancements have dramatically reduced the physical hardware requirements for a commercially viable system.
    * **Milestone 5 is the New Milestone 6:** Previously, Google estimated a commercial system would require 1 million physical qubits (Milestone 6). Due to algorithmic efficiency, a commercially relevant machine is now projected to require only **100,000 physical qubits** (Milestone 5).
* **First Useful Quantum Algorithm:** Google, in partnership with UC Berkeley, demonstrated **Quantum Echoes**, the first quantum machine learning algorithm applied to a real-world scientific task.
    * **Chemical Discovery:** The algorithm was used to analyze nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) data to solve an open chemistry question: measuring the dihedral rotation angles of diphenyl molecules.

## The Bidirectional Synergy of "Quantum AI"
* **AI Accelerating Quantum:** Artificial intelligence is being utilized to solve complex quantum engineering tasks.
    * **AlphaQubits:** A collaboration between Google DeepMind and the Quantum AI team applied machine learning to significantly optimize quantum error correction decoding.
* **Quantum Accelerating AI:** Quantum computers can generate synthetic datasets to train classical AI models in domains where real-world data collection is bottlenecked.
    * **Data Generation:** While projects like AlphaFold required 50 years of physical data collection to train, a quantum computer can simulate molecular and material science data rapidly. Google has already begun sharing quantum-generated material science datasets with DeepMind.

## Cryptanalysis and the Post-Quantum Timeline
* **The Threat to Current Encryption:** Quantum computers running Shor’s algorithm can crack modern cryptographic standards, such as RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), by easily solving complex mathematical factoring problems.
* **Collapsing Timelines:** Refinements in quantum algorithms have drastically lowered the estimated hardware size required to break encryption standards.
    * **RSA-2048:** The estimated physical qubit requirement to crack RSA-2048 has dropped from 20 million to just 1 million.
    * **ECC-256:** Digital signatures and cryptocurrencies using ECC-256 could be compromised with only a few hundred thousand physical qubits.
* **The 2029 Target:** Google has published guidelines advising organizations that they must transition to post-quantum cryptographic schemes by **2029** to protect against future quantum decryptional capabilities.

***

> "Temperature is really the physicist's term for noise, and we don't want to have noise in our chips. So the colder we can make it, the better." — Hartmut Neven

> "A real powerful future AI wants to have access... to the most potent, capable computational substrate we can think of, and currently that is quantum computing." — Hartmut Neven

> "Because of this progress, advances in algorithms, we now think that a commercially relevant machine would only need about 100,000 physical qubits... milestone five is the new milestone six." — Hartmut Neven

briefings.title: Google I/O 2026, Karpathy Joins Anthropic, and Cerebras’ $95B IPO | EP #256
briefings.tldr: Google I/O showcased the tech giant’s massive transition into an AI-native operating system powered by an expected $180B–$190B annual CapEx, while Cerebras Systems CEO Andrew Feldman celebrated a historic $95 billion IPO, highlighting a massive market shift toward custom, wafer-scale high-throughput inference chips.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Google I/O showcased the tech giant’s massive transition into an AI-native operating system powered by an expected $180B–$190B annual CapEx, while Cerebras Systems CEO Andrew Feldman celebrated a historic $95 billion IPO, highlighting a massive market shift toward custom, wafer-scale high-throughput inference chips.

---

## Google I/O: Astronomical Scale, High Throughput, and Ambient Search

*   **Massive Infrastructure CapEx:** Google is scaling its annual CapEx to an estimated $180 billion to $190 billion (up 6x from $31 billion in 2022) to support a global network running more than 1 million custom TPUs. 
*   **Unparalleled Token Growth:** Google’s monthly token processing jumped 7x year-over-year to 3.2 quadrillion tokens, with model APIs now processing 19 billion tokens per minute. The consumer Gemini app has reached 900 million active monthly users.
*   **Gemini 3.5 Flash:** Launched as the new default model for Gemini and AI Search, Flash focuses heavily on raw speed (boasting 4x faster output than competing frontier models) and tool orchestration over raw frontier intelligence benchmarks.
*   **Gemini Omni & Deep Multimodality:** Led by DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis, GDM is pushing deep multimodal video and audio generation (such as generating custom, physics-accurate claymation explainer videos of protein folding), positioning Google as the sole US frontier lab heavily chasing video and physical-world simulations.
*   **Verification via SynthID:** To counter synthetic misinformation, Google's SynthID has watermarked over 100 billion images and 60,000 years of audio. Major AI platforms, including OpenAI, Kakao, and ElevenLabs, have officially adopted the standard.
*   **AI-Native Search & Universal Cart:** Google Search is transitioning to a persistent model where user-defined AI agents continuously crawl web, social, and forum data in the background (e.g., tracking rental listings). Additionally, a "Universal Cart" will allow users to seamlessly add products, track prices, and purchase items across YouTube, Gmail, Search, and partner merchants like Nike, Target, and Shopify.

## The Agentic Shift and Consumer Hardware Pivots

*   **Anti-gravity 2.0:** Rebranded from the Windsurf acquisition, Google's new standalone, agent-first developer environment automates complex software engineering tasks by orchestrating fleets of code agents in parallel, pointing toward a future where code is entirely abstracted away from human developers.
*   **Gemini Spark:** Powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash, Spark is Google’s always-on personal agent that runs 24/7 on dedicated Google Cloud virtual machines. It automates cross-product actions like scanning Gmail inboxes, managing Calendar invites, and building live trackers in Google Sheets.
*   **Samsung & Google Audio Glasses:** Arriving this fall, these glasses use Gemini to whisper private audio assistance directly into the user's ear. Featuring frames co-designed by Warby Parker and Gentle Monster, the glasses opt for an audio-only interface to preserve battery life and maintain real-world user presence.

## Cerebras Systems’ Historic $95B IPO and Wafer-Scale Innovation

*   **Historic Valuation & Market Debut:** Cerebras Systems completed the largest US tech IPO since Uber in 2019, raising $5.5 billion, closing up 68%, and reaching a $95 billion market cap.
*   **The Wafer-Scale Bet:** Co-founder and CEO Andrew Feldman detailed the company’s highly contrarian architecture: bypassing traditional GPUs to build a single dinner-plate-sized wafer (58x larger than normal chips) packed with 40 to 50 gigabytes of ultra-fast SRAM rather than slower HBM or DRAM.
*   **Performance Leaps:** By keeping model memory entirely on-wafer, Cerebras runs inference workloads up to 15x to 20x faster than traditional GPU setups, achieving 1,000 tokens per second on trillion-parameter open-source models like Llama-3-based architectures.
*   **Massive Enterprise Validation:** Cerebras scaled from selling 12 systems in Gen 1 to thousands in Gen 3. In December 2025, they signed a landmark multi-year deal with OpenAI worth over $20 billion, followed by a major deployment term sheet with AWS in March.
*   **The Domestic Manufacturing Bottleneck:** Feldman emphasized that building semiconductor fabs is a decades-long endeavor. He estimates Elon Musk’s proposed domestic "Terafab" to be a 15-to-20-year project due to the immense complexity of manufacturing and advanced packaging, which is currently concentrated in Taiwan and South Korea.

## Key AI Personnel Moves and Legal Milestones

*   **Andre Karpathy Joins Anthropic:** The OpenAI co-founder and former Tesla FSD head joined Anthropic's pre-training team to use Claude to accelerate its own pre-training research. Karpathy noted that researchers who remain outside of frontier labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) inevitably experience "judgment drift" as the cutting edge becomes too opaque.
*   **OpenAI Defeats Musk Lawsuit:** A federal jury unanimously rejected Elon Musk’s breach-of-contract lawsuit against OpenAI in just two hours, ruling that Musk waited too long to file under the statute of limitations. Feldman characterized the legal battle as a "giant distraction" that diverted focus from constructive development.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "When we look back at this time, I think we'll realize that we were standing in the foothills of the singularity." 
> — Demis Hassabis, Co-founder and CEO of Google DeepMind

> "It's like a lifetime achievement, like kind of like a Nobel Prize or an Olympic gold medal, where you carry it for the rest of your life."
> — Andrew Feldman, Co-founder and CEO of Cerebras Systems (on ringing the IPO bell)

> "I'm a professional David in the battle with Goliath. This is what I know how to do... I have no interest in working with people who are other than those who want to attack the hardest problems."
> — Andrew Feldman, Co-founder and CEO of Cerebras Systems

briefings.title: How to Build a Self-Improving Company with AI
briefings.tldr: Instead of using AI as a mere productivity "copilot" within traditional corporate hierarchies, founders should design their companies as a series of autonomous, recursive AI loops that self-improve overnight by operating on fully recorded, legible organizational knowledge.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
Instead of using AI as a mere productivity "copilot" within traditional corporate hierarchies, founders should design their companies as a series of autonomous, recursive AI loops that self-improve overnight by operating on fully recorded, legible organizational knowledge.

## Beyond Copilots: Reimagining the Company Structure

*   **The Roman Legion Fallacy:** Traditional corporate structures operate like Roman legions—nested hierarchies where humans serve as the primary conduits for passing orders down and information up. AI fundamentally breaks this assumption.
*   **The Copilot Misconception:** Treating AI as a "copilot" to make employees 20% more productive is a flawed approach. It merely bolts a faster engine onto an obsolete way of working. 
*   **Extracting Domain Knowledge:** The true power of AI lies in centralizing and extracting "know-how" from Slack messages, emails, Notion, and recordings, and packaging it into a unified context or set of skills that an AI agent can autonomously act upon.

## The Recursive, Self-Improving AI Loop

*   **The Five-Layer Autonomous Loop:** To build a system that improves while you sleep, companies must link five core layers without human bottlenecks:
    *   **Sensor Layer:** Captures real-world inputs (customer emails, support tickets, cancellations, product telemetry).
    *   **Policy/Decision Layer:** Governs rules, guardrails, and parameters for when the AI must ask a human for permission.
    *   **Tool Layer:** Deterministic APIs and code execution (e.g., querying databases, checking calendars).
    *   **Quality Gate:** Evaluates safety filters, deterministic checks, and human review for high-risk actions.
    *   **Learning Mechanism:** Analyzes failures and successes to feed back into the top of the loop.
*   **The "Holy Shit" YC Milestone:** YC built an agent to query its internal database. They added a monitoring agent that reviewed every failed search, identified missing indexes or code, wrote a merge request to the YC codebase, had an AI agent review it, and deployed it overnight. When employees logged in the next day, the system had autonomously fixed its own software bugs.
*   **Self-Optimizing Business Functions:**
    *   *Product Analytics:* AI agents can continuously review sales funnels, identify friction points, design and run A/B tests, and deploy the winning version.
    *   *Customer Support to Code:* An AI agent acting as "CPO/CTO" can triage user feedback, identify features aligned with the roadmap, write the code, and ship it to production overnight without human intervention.

## Structural and Operational Implications

*   **Burn Tokens, Not Headcount:** YC startups are reaching Demo Day with roughly **5x more revenue per employee** than they did 18 months ago. 
    *   *Token Maxing:* Startups should measure and optimize for token usage rather than headcount.
*   **The End of Middle Management:** Coordination-heavy middle management roles are no longer necessary. Effective organizations will consist of only two core human roles:
    *   *Individual Contributors (ICs):* Hands-on builders and operators.
    *   *Directly Responsible Individuals (DRIs):* A single, named human (not a committee) accountable for driving specific outcomes.

## Legibility and Ephemeral Software

*   **Making the Organization Legible:** To leverage AI, every email, Slack DM, and partner conversation must be recorded, transcribed, and diarized. 
    *   *The Rule of Legibility:* "If it did not get recorded, it did not happen to your intelligence."
*   **The Living YC User Manual:** YC General Partner Harj took 2,000 hours of recorded office hours from a three-month period, diarized and categorized the transcripts, and used AI to generate a brand-new, 150-page YC User Manual over a single weekend. This manual now self-improves dynamically as new office hours are recorded.
*   **Software as an Ephemeral Asset:** With advanced code generation (e.g., Codex 55), internal dashboards and software tools should be treated as entirely disposable. 
    *   *Data Preservation vs. Software Ephemerality:* Companies should meticulously preserve business data and context but generate, throw away, and regenerate the software interfaces on top of them as underlying AI models improve.

## Where Humans Still Matter

*   **Humans on the Edge:** In a self-improving company, the AI functions as the central "company brain" while humans operate on the periphery, interfacing with the real world where models cannot yet reach.
*   **High-Stakes and Emotional Contexts:** Human intervention remains critical for:
    *   Novel, unmapped situations and ethical considerations.
    *   High-stakes, high-emotion scenarios (such as resolving co-founder disputes).
    *   B2B sales and relationship-building conversations.

## Notable Quotes

> "AI isn't something you bolt onto the side of a company... I think you can reimagine what a company is as a set of recursive, self-improving AI loops." — Tom Blomfield

> "If it is recorded, it happened to the AI. If it did not get recorded, it did not happen to your intelligence." — Tom Blomfield

> "I think the business context and skills are the valuable part. I think the software on top of it is ephemeral." — Tom Blomfield

briefings.title: Notion’s Ivan Zhao: The Refounder
briefings.tldr: Notion co-founder and CEO Ivan Zhao and Sequoia's Brian Halligan discuss "jazz mode"—a decentralized, adaptive approach to organizational design that enables companies to run like improvisational bands rather than rigid marching bands.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Notion co-founder and CEO Ivan Zhao and Sequoia's Brian Halligan discuss "jazz mode"—a decentralized, adaptive approach to organizational design that enables companies to run like improvisational bands rather than rigid marching bands. By leveraging a barbell-shaped engineering team, prioritizing "taste" and agency over experience, and executing radical "re-foundings," Notion demonstrates how legacy SaaS companies can successfully transition into fast-moving, AI-native enterprises.

---

## "Jazz Mode" and Rethinking the Org Chart
* **The Jazz Band Philosophy:** Ivan Zhao describes Notion’s operating model as a "jazz band, not a marching band." Instead of marching in a rigid, top-down formation, the organization relies on high autonomy, self-equilibrium, and individual improvisation to stay agile.
* **The Invariance of Hierarchy:** While AI allows organizations to become flatter, Zhao argues that fully flat structures run contrary to human nature. He asserts that organizations will remain hierarchical because human beings are biologically wired for division of labor and hierarchical grouping.
* **The "Circle" Org Chart:** Host Brian Halligan notes a structural shift from the traditional "triangle" org chart to a "circle" org chart. In this model, centralized AI systems sit in the middle, aggregating complete company context. Humans act as trainers feeding the system context and taste, allowing the AI to gradually automate micro-decision-making.
* **Leveraging Ex-Founders:** Notion maintains a staff of roughly 50 to 60 ex-founders. This high density of entrepreneurial talent enables decentralized leadership, allowing team members to cross organizational boundaries and drive cross-functional projects without territorial friction.

## Evolving Talent Profiles and the "Barbell" Engineering Team
* **The Barbell Team Structure:** Rather than hiring mid-level talent, Notion has structured its engineering organization into a distinct barbell shape:
    * **Super-Junior ICs:** Energetic, high-agency, out-of-school individual contributors (ICs) who can scale their output rapidly using AI coding agents.
    * **Super-Senior Architects:** Highly experienced engineers who provide structural direction, systems design, and "taste"—skills that language models cannot replicate. They manage junior engineers, who in turn manage multiple coding agents.
* **Hiring for Taste and Will:** Traditional hiring metrics prioritized "slope" (pure cognitive speed) and experience. Because AI has democratized and normalized capabilities like writing and programming, Notion now hires based on a different formula: $\text{Talent} = (\text{Capability/Experience}) \times \text{Taste} (Value System) \times \text{Will} (Agency/Work Ethic)$. 
* **The Elimination of the CMO:** Notion dismantled its traditional CMO organization, splitting it into two distinct, decentralized functions:
    * **Storytelling:** Placed directly adjacent to product and social media channels to match rapid product-shipping cadences.
    * **Demand Generation:** Aligned directly under sales to focus on lead generation and go-to-market execution.
* **No-Resume First Rounds:** For sales hires, Notion's first-round evaluation bypasses traditional resumes. Candidates are instead required to physically build and submit something using Notion to demonstrate their hands-on product alignment.

## The Art of "Re-founding"
* **Re-founding Twice:** Zhao is a proponent of radical self-reinvention, having guided Notion through two crucial pivots:
    * **Kyoto (2015):** Lacking product-market fit and running out of cash, Zhao and co-founder Simon Last laid off their small team, sublet their San Francisco office to become cash-flow positive, and relocated to Kyoto, Japan. They spent a year and a half living together and rebuilding Notion's codebase from scratch.
    * **Cancun (2023):** Upon receiving early access to GPT-4—which Zhao described as a "full-body religious experience"—the team gathered in Mexico to pivot Notion into an AI-first company.
* **Decalcifying through M&A:** To prevent organizational calcification as the company grew to over 1,000 employees, Notion intentionally used acquisitions and acquihires to bring in aggressive, external startup founders who challenge legacy internal thinking.
* **Transitioning to "Wartime":** Zhao and Halligan agree that the SaaS industry has entered a "wartime" era. Financial planning remains conservative and metric-driven, but product planning is conducted week-by-week rather than on 3- or 6-month cycles to keep pace with rapid market changes.

## Building with AI: Brewing Beer vs. Engineering Bridges
* **Software as Brewing Beer:** Zhao notes that traditional software development is like "engineering a bridge" (highly predictable and design-led). Building with LLMs is like "brewing beer" (unpredictable, dependent on active experimentation, and reliant on throwing top talent at a model to see what flavor profiles emerge).
* **AI as "Organizational Steel":** Zhao compares LLMs to structural steel in architecture. Before steel, buildings were limited to six stories; similarly, AI paired with software acts as "steel" for modern organizations, allowing them to scale taller and faster without being crushed by communication overhead.
* **Gross Margin Dynamics:** While running AI products can negatively impact gross margins due to heavy GPU and token consumption, Zhao explains that knowledge-management platforms can mitigate this. Unlike coding products that require top-tier frontier models, knowledge tasks (e.g., filing IT tickets or search queries) can be effectively routed to cheaper, second-tier, or open-weight models.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "We start a mantra in the company, 'We want to be a jazz band, not a marching band.'" — Ivan Zhao

> "Building classic software is like engineering a bridge. If you can design it, you usually can build it, fairly predictable... Building with language models back then and somewhat still is, is like brewing beer. You can't truly predict things." — Ivan Zhao

> "Taste is not in language models... Taste is more rooted based on your value system. Are you drinking sparkling water or still water? Are you drinking Diet Coke or iced tea? To each of their own, there's no right answers." — Ivan Zhao

> "If you're stuck, and a lot of companies are stuck, be risk-on and do what Ivan did, like, he was a ye old SaaS company and now he's a rocket ship AI company." — Brian Halligan

briefings.title: Powell Is Out, Warsh Is In: What It Means for Crypto
briefings.tldr: As Kevin Warsh prepares to succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve Chair, global bond yields signal severe macro tightening while stock markets reach all-time highs on AI hype.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
As Kevin Warsh prepares to succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve Chair, global bond yields signal severe macro tightening while stock markets reach all-time highs on AI hype. Meanwhile, the crypto sector is adjusting to major structural shifts, highlighted by Coinbase’s strategic alignment with Hyperliquid to boost global USDC distribution and anticipation of the U.S. Clarity Act.

---

## The Divergence: Stock Market Hype vs. Bond Market Reality
*   **A Growing Valuation Gap:** Global bond yields are climbing, signaling global tightening, while the stock market continues to reach new highs.
    *   **The Equal-Weight Discrepancy:** The gap between the market-cap-weighted S&P 500 and the equal-weight index is widening at a rate not seen since 1999, right before the dot-com bust, indicating an incredibly top-heavy market.
    *   **The AI Momentum:** The stock market remains swept up in hype cycles, particularly around AI and chip sectors like Nvidia. Acheson warns that forward P/E ratios are based on company guidance that assumes endless infrastructure demand, creating underlying market fragility. 
*   **Sticky Inflation Indicators:** Core CPI has hovered flatly between 2.6% and 3.0% since 2024, proving that disinflation has stalled.
    *   **The Hormuz Crisis Legacy:** Even if the Strait of Hormuz crisis resolves, it will take months for energy price declines to filter through to core inflation indices.
    *   **Gas Price Psychology:** In the U.S., rising pump prices drive up consumer inflation expectations, which in turn influences actual inflation behavior.

## The "BLISS Trade" and Fiscal Moral Hazard
*   **Structural Stimulus over the "Trump Trade":** Former IMF Chief Economist Gita Gopinath coined the term **BLISS** ("Big, Large, and Sustained Stimulus") to describe a structural shift in global governance.
    *   **No Pain Allowed:** Regardless of political party, modern administrations will spend aggressively to bail out citizens and markets from banking crises, energy spikes, or market crashes to avoid being voted out of office.
*   **Currency Debasement Speculation:** The certainty of this permanent safety net (the "Fed Put") encourages high-risk speculation while driving long-term currency debasement. This makes hard assets like Bitcoin highly attractive long-term debasement hedges.

## Fed Leadership Transition: Powell Out, Warsh In
*   **Jerome Powell’s Mixed Legacy:** Powell's tenure was marked by massive crises, including the 2019 repo crisis, the pandemic, and historic inflation.
    *   **The Inflation Blindspot:** Powell heavily damaged Fed credibility by mischaracterizing early inflation as "transitory."
    *   **Crypto Debanking:** Powell was behind the regulatory pressure that led to the debanking of crypto firms and the eventual collapse of Silvergate Bank in March 2023.
*   **Kevin Warsh's New Playbook:** Incoming Fed Chair Kevin Warsh faces a challenging high-inflation environment.
    *   **Reduced Forward Guidance:** Warsh wants to move away from "spoon-feeding" the market, which may result in fewer FOMC press conferences and dot plots, forcing analysts to reintroduce original thinking.
    *   **The Rate Outlook:** Acheson predicts "no cuts and no hikes" in the immediate future. While a consensus has formed around no rate cuts, expectations of a rate hike are overblown given current economic uncertainties. 

## Crypto Markets: Coinbase-Hyperliquid Alliance and the Clarity Act
*   **Coinbase and Hyperliquid's Strategic Alignment:** Coinbase has significantly increased its position in staked HYPE, signaling deep institutional cooperation despite being natural competitors.
    *   **USDC Distribution Play:** While Coinbase operates as a compliant, US-centric institution, it is leveraging Hyperliquid’s non-KYC, global perpetuals platform to grow international distribution of USDC.
    *   **Neutralizing Competition:** For Coinbase and Circle, installing themselves as collateral managers for Hyperliquid is a highly strategic move to capture recurring net interest income.
*   **The Clarity Act Catalyst:** Acheson believes the Clarity Act has a reasonable chance of passing this year.
    *   **Ethereum and DeFi Benefit:** While Bitcoin already possesses regulatory clarity, the bill would provide a massive regulatory unlock for Ethereum, staking, and decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). 
    *   **Market Price-In:** The regulatory progress is not fully priced into crypto markets due to a prolonged retail malaise, leaving room for a significant market jump if the bill is signed into law.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "The stock market is being driven... by intrinsic and temporary factors, excitement about AI mainly... whereas the bond market looks at the macro outlook... That's why [we have] two very different drummers, not painting the same story, but they don't need to." — Noelle Acheson

> "The BLISS trade, which is 'Big, Large, and Sustained Stimulus' or support, is structural. Her [Gita Gopinath's] point is that there is no administration now that will not spend to get people out of difficulties... Governments are not going to be voted out of office because they are not spending to save people." — Noelle Acheson

> "Inflation kills societies, and if we don't keep an eye on it, then there could be some very bad scenarios going ahead. Inflation will dictate monetary policy; inflation will have a very big impact on fiscal policy at a global level... You can massage the indices, but you can't hide from inflation." — Noelle Acheson

briefings.title: Sundar Pichai on Agents Replacing Engineers, Google's Future, AI's Flip Phone Moment, and More
briefings.tldr: Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlights a rapid shift toward proactive, personalized AI agents that will make today’s technology look primitive within three years, emphasizing that Google’s strategy remains deeply "creator-first" and focused on enhancing human productivity rather than replacing human connection.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlights a rapid shift toward proactive, personalized AI agents that will make today’s technology look primitive within three years, emphasizing that Google’s strategy remains deeply "creator-first" and focused on enhancing human productivity rather than replacing human connection.

***

## The "Flip Phone" Moment and the Shift to AI Agents
* **The Three-Year Outlook:** Pichai predicts that the pace of AI advancement is on a steep curve; in three years, today's cutting-edge AI models will be viewed as "primitive," akin to looking back at a flip phone.
* **Proactive, Cross-Device Intelligence:** 
    * **Continuous Context:** Google is building personal intelligence that runs 24/7 in Google Cloud, syncing context across laptops, phones, and watches. 
    * **User Control:** To balance this deep personalization, Google is implementing strict user controls, including incognito modes and the ability to pause agent activity.
* **The Shift to Agentic Action:** With platforms like Spark, the value of AI is shifting from static benchmarks to "agentic" capabilities—taking on complex, multi-step real-world tasks (e.g., planning a trip, organizing weekly groceries) to free up human time for more meaningful experiences.
* **Fluid Modality:** The future of content consumption will allow any input modality (text, audio, video) to seamlessly translate to any other modality, fundamentally changing how users interact with information.

## YouTube’s "Creator-First" AI Strategy
* **Human-to-Human Priority:** In contrast to competitors aiming for fully AI-generated social feeds, Pichai emphasizes that YouTube’s strategy remains firmly "creator-first." The core value of the platform lies in the authentic connection between creators and their audiences.
* **Creative Force Multipliers:** Generative tools like Veo, Omni, and YouTube's Flow are designed to democratize high-end production. Pichai compares this shift to the introduction of CGI, noting it will allow independent creators—even high school students—to produce movie-quality content.
* **Navigating Creator Concerns:**
    * **Protecting Watch Time:** Regarding features like "Ask YouTube" (which allows viewers to query and compare videos), Google is testing carefully to ensure these tools drive deeper engagement and pull more complex search queries into the ecosystem rather than cannibalizing creator watch time.
    * **Creator Education:** Acknowledging that some creators fear audience backlash for using AI, Pichai highlighted the need for better education on tools like auto-dubbing, which dramatically expand a creator's global reach.

## The Future of Software Engineering and Agentic Coding
* **Beyond Auto-Completion:** While 75% of new code at Google is currently generated with AI assistance, Pichai states that simple code completion is no longer the true frontier.
* **Orchestrating Teams of Agents:** The role of the software engineer is shifting toward agent management and orchestration. Rather than just writing lines of code, engineers will manage fleets of specialized sub-agents to execute complex, long-running tasks.
* **Automated Code Migration:** Google is already utilizing "agentic coding" internally to tackle massive infrastructure projects, such as deploying agent fleets to migrate complex codebases between languages (e.g., converting C++ to Rust, or Python to Go) using the existing binary as the technical specification.

## Navigating Rapid Change: Advice for the Next Generation
* **Managing Technological Anxiety:** Pichai acknowledges that humans are not naturally wired for the current velocity of technological change. 
* **Continuous Learning Mindset:** He advises young people to focus on continuous adaptation, treating AI tools as personal learning accelerators—similar to how previous generations used YouTube to self-educate.
* **The Enduring Value of College:** Despite the rise of self-directed digital learning, Pichai still recommends attending college for its role in personal growth, developing deep social networks, and fostering critical life skills.

***

## Notable Quotes

> "I'm very confident three years from now you will look back at what we had today and you will realize they were like, pretty primitive. It's like looking at a flip phone." — Sundar Pichai

> "Ultimately, the power of these tools comes from freeing up some of the tasks you do so that you're spending your time more meaningfully on whatever you want to do." — Sundar Pichai

> "The new metric is going to be what tasks did you get done by just deploying agents. Engineers—each engineer will have these many, many agents at their disposal." — Sundar Pichai

> "I think particularly in YouTube, we are going to be very creator-first... At the end of the day, the human-to-human connection is always there, that's how I think about it." — Sundar Pichai
